newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy repo rate fall not seen as rate cut signal.
newsitem.headline: Italy repo rate fall not seen as rate cut signal.

text.p: A fall in Italy's lira repurchase rate to 8.22 percent at Thursday's tender, taking it below the 8.25 percent discount rate, does not signify that official rates are set for an imminent cut, banking sources said.
At the Bank of Italy's repo operation earlier on Thursday, the minimum rate fell to 8.22 from 8.53 percent previously and the average rate fell to 8.26 percent from 8.55.
"The Bank of Italy did not want to signal a change. The operation is a very short term one and so the indication you can draw from the rate is only relative," a banking source said.
The repo pact was for five days, compared with 15 days at the last operation on September 16.
